_comment: Live-stream tuning. Intervals are in seconds and are what the scheduler AIMS for;
the poller widens them automatically under two conditions:
1. bandwidth  - if a source exceeds max_mb_per_min, its interval is stretched
to fit the budget rather than the budget being ignored.
2. failure    - a circuit breaker backs a failing source off exponentially.
Every wire size below was measured on 2026-07-30, gzip where the source supports it.
The MCX story is the important one. Its market-watch call returns the ENTIRE option
chain - 1,277,049 bytes, uncompressed, no ETag, no Last-Modified, and it ignores
Accept-Encoding entirely. At 2s that is 38 MB/min = 32 GB/day and a near-certain IP ban.
The heatmap endpoint carries the same 16 major futures (GOLD, SILVER, CRUDEOIL,
NATURALGAS, COPPER, ZINC, ALUMINIUM, LEAD, NICKEL, MENTHAOIL + mini/petal variants)
with LTP, OHLC, volume and open interest in 4,795 bytes - 266x smaller. So the fast
loop uses the heatmap, and the full market watch runs every 15 minutes purely to
refresh the complete contract list, units and expiries.

bse_quotes.label: BSE watchlist
bse_quotes.note: No bulk endpoint: the whole watchlist is fetched in parallel each cycle, 594b per scrip.

mcx_heatmap.label: MCX futures heatmap
mcx_heatmap.note: The fast MCX loop. 16 major futures with LTP/OHLC/OI.

mcx_full.label: MCX full market watch
mcx_full.note: 1.28MB uncompressed. Slow loop only - contract list, units, expiries. NEVER put this on the fast path.

broker_stocks.label: Broker stocks
broker_stocks.note: 18 listed brokers and broker parents, quoted via BSE getScripHeaderData. 594b per scrip.
